title: Register changes that record the classified V2-E02A runs, V2-S7-002-PR1
description: What V2-S7-002-PR1 changed in the register to record the three runs of V2-E02A: every register change with its value before and after, the finding each answers, and the review artifacts the changes rest on. The runs, e02a-1, e02a-2, and e02a-3, executed on 2026-10-31 in V2-S7-001-PR2, which registered no claim. This ledger is written on 2026-11-01, after the classification and after the independent review of the runs. It is the seventh ledger written after v1.0.0 was released, and like the six before it, it is not part of the pack that release was cut over: the evidence index undoes it, with the other post-release ledgers, to recompute that pack. It adds one claim, certified at C2 on the three records it adds with it, and replaces one surface reason. A claim status is a governed decision, and the level of a record does not make a claim certified: the repository owner chose on 2026-11-01 to register this claim in this change, knowing that adding this ledger changes tools/evidence_index, a pinned input of the latest freeze records. No tool reads that choice.

claim.statement: In three runs on 2026-10-31, on the docker-desktop provider, on one cluster with one node, at the commit ff45093b2a9bf2cdbcde5fee453fbc6b64f2e53b, under revision 4 of the V2-E02A freeze record, a release with two API replicas and one runtime replica served the real model while the RP-1 caller sent requests through the API Service, and the control deleted the one runtime pod once in each run. In each run two requests failed, in one failure episode of 3,682 ms to 4,276 ms that the analysis starts about 30 s after the fault, and the largest time between two successes is 29,893 ms to 30,427 ms. The seven validity criteria of the record hold in each run, so each is PASSED, which states that the run is valid and not that the service stayed available. The set meets the comparison eligibility rule of the record on its failure episodes.
claim.limitation: Runtime, C2, about three runs, e02a-1, e02a-2, and e02a-3, at one commit, on one provider, docker-desktop, on one cluster with one node on Kubernetes v1.36.1, with one release, one model, and one caller workload. The state of each run rests on a reading of E02A-AC2 that the repository owner approved on 2026-10-31, after the evidence was read: the freeze record does not state that reading, no tool reads the approval, and on the readings of the runtime readyReplicas count no run would be counted and this claim would not stand. The eligibility rests on the failure episodes alone. The zero-Ready condition holds on the first reading that gave zero and not on the outer start, and the record does not state which applies. The start of a failure episode is the completion of its first failed request: the failed requests were in flight for most of the time with no completion, and the caller failure episode does not hold that time. The failure count is 2 in each run, and the caller profile has 2 workers. The model file of each replacement pod was not compared directly. The host paged, and no record establishes whether that changed a figure. The review of the result is a record of a separate session of the same assistant, and no person and no outside party reviewed the result. It read no register statement about these runs, it ran no tool of this repository, and it does not establish that this claim is correct. Registration, 2026-11-01: V2-S7-001-PR2 ran the three runs and registered no claim. V2-S7-002-PR1 classified them and added this claim. No run executed in that change, and no file of a run changed.
claim.doesNotEstablish: That the service stayed available; that one runtime replica is or is not acceptable for any service; a comparison with two runtime replicas, an improvement, or a percentage, since no run of V2-E02B exists; an authorization of a run of V2-E02B or of a change of the desired state; node failure, overload, sustained capacity, or production availability; the cause of a failure, of a gap, or of a recovery; a figure of the V1 pod-loss evidence; that the model file of a replacement pod is the file of the record; that paging on the host changed no figure; a service-level objective; behaviour on another provider, Kubernetes version, node count, release, or caller workload; representative evidence, C3, or operational evidence, C4; a cost, a saving, a return on investment, or a business effect; that a person reviewed the result; or production readiness.

evidenceRecords.summary: On 2026-10-31 run e02a-1 of V2-E02A ran as revision 4 of its freeze record registers it, at the merged commit ff45093b2a9bf2cdbcde5fee453fbc6b64f2e53b, on the docker-desktop provider, with two API replicas and one runtime replica. The control deleted the one runtime pod once while RP-1 ran. 2 of 365 requests in the window failed, in one failure episode of 4276 ms, the largest time between two successes is 29896 ms, and the runtime tier has one zero-Ready interval with an inner figure of 17342 ms and an outer figure of 26813 ms. The seven validity criteria hold on the reading of E02A-AC2 that the repository owner approved, and the state is PASSED.

Revision 4 names this environment by the identity sha256:6a219b3ff959a0020d982d967abeed6696aa0f0d1b594bdf3ad86b9aeda8cd5c, and each capacity reading of the run states that identity.

measurement.method: The caller record states each request. The timeline collector read the endpoints, pods, deployments, and argo streams. tools/reliability_analysis computed each figure from those files, and tools/analysis_replay binds the result to the evidence.
measurement.instrument: The reliability runner, the timeline collector, the telemetry collector, the operator event log, and the reliability analysis.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The control deleted exactly the pod that the rule of fault.target selected (the first Ready runtime pod by name), once, by name: commands.txt holds one delete command, the fault-injection-started event names that pod, and a pods reading after the event shows that UID with a deletion timestamp or absent. No other pod of the release has a deletion timestamp before the end of the observation, except a pod that the Deployment controller removes.

The endpoints, pods, deployments, and argo streams are each accepted by their reader, each states a value in its first and its last reading inside the window, and each has at most 10 s between two consecutive readings with a value inside the window.

The caller record is accepted by its reader with the plan, in the mode in-cluster, with the API Service as its target and the end state duration. It covers the window, its last completion before the window succeeded, so the window does not start inside a failure episode, and at least one request completes inside the window after the fault-injection-finished event.

Either a pod of the tier of the fault with a UID that no pod had before the fault is Ready in a pods reading and the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, or the observation limit is reached. The result page states which.

When the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, at least 10 successful requests complete after the stabilizedAt instant inside the window, and the last of them completes at least 60 s after it.
No unrelated failure occurs inside the window: no container of a pod that the fault did not target restarts, no pod that the fault did not target is replaced, and the node stays Ready.

Every file that evidencePaths lists is present and named by the manifest, the operator event log is closed, python -m tools.experiment_evidence check accepts the run directory, and python -m tools.analysis_replay verify reproduces its run analysis.

results.statement: commands.txt holds one fault phase of the driver, and control.json states the one delete command of pod/inferops-inferops-llm-runtime-6b4554dc64-l7tth. The first pods reading after the event shows its UID with a deletion timestamp. No other listed pod has one.

On the readings of each stream, each of the four streams answered each reading inside the window, and the largest time between two readings is 4.911 s. The repository owner approved that reading on 2026-10-31, after the evidence was read. On the readings of the runtime readyReplicas count alone, the largest time is 25.1 s.

The caller record has the mode in-cluster, the API Service as its target, and the end state duration, and it covers the window. 332 requests complete inside the window after fault-injection-finished, by more than the margin.
A runtime pod with a new UID is Ready in pods.jsonl from 13:41:57.659Z. The analysis states a stabilized recovery at 2026-10-31T13:43:11.618Z, inside the observation limit.
295 successful requests complete after stabilizedAt inside the window, and the last completes 621.663 s after it.

pods.jsonl states no restart of any listed container. The two API pods are the same in each reading. transcript.txt holds 21 reads of the node, and each states Ready True. Those reads are samples, and they do not read each instant of the window.

Each file of the evidence paths is present and named by the manifest, and the event log is closed. python -m tools.experiment_evidence check accepts the run directory, and python -m tools.analysis_replay verify reproduces its run analysis.

registerChanges.reason: Three runs executed under the merged revision 4, each is PASSED on the reading of E02A-AC2 that the repository owner approved, the set is classified, and a review record of each run is in the state the index is built from. The register states what those three runs show, at C2, in a claim of its own, bounded to the environment the runs record. The claim is appended to the register, so no existing pointer into it moves. The status is certified: three executed records support the statement inside the boundary that its limitation states. That is a claim status, and it is not a reliability result: the statement says that requests failed.

before.reason: Contribution and review convention. It states how a change is validated and how evidence is labelled, and asserts no capability.
Repository governance for this skeleton. It describes how the repository is run rather than what the software does.
The index of accepted decisions. Each ADR is a decision; the capabilities they enable are claimed by the rows above.
